reason: The hypothesis directly restates the known result from P24 and other passages that Mn forms a non-protective MnO scale under low oxygen partial pressure and a more protective spinel under higher pO2, and that a defective scale causes internal oxidation and failure. It applies this well-known behavior to a slightly different alloy composition (Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3) without providing a new mechanistic link or resolving any conflict between sources; the proposed test is a standard comparative oxidation experiment.
copied_elements: Mn forms MnO under low pO2 (P24, P15)
Mn forms MnCr2O4 spinel under higher pO2 (P22, P23)
Al2O3 forms as inner protective layer (P2, P4, P6)
porous/defective scale leads to internal oxidation and cracking (P14, P22)
catastrophic failure from oxide cracking and spallation (P14, P29)
varying oxygen partial pressure changes oxide type and protectiveness (P24)
high-temperature exposure at 900°C and above (P9, P12, P14, P29)
